'''''Ledger''''' is the first [[peer-reviewed]] [[academic journal]] dedicated to [[cryptocurrency]] and [[blockchain technology]] research.<ref name="Extance2015">{{cite journal |last1=Extance |first1=Andy |title=The future of cryptocurrencies: Bitcoin and beyond |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |volume=526 |issue=7571 |year=2015 |pages=21–23 |doi=10.1038/526021a |bibcode=2015Natur.526...21E |pmid=26432223|doi-access=free }}</ref>
The journal covers topics that relate to cryptocurrencies such as [[bitcoin]].  This includes aspects of mathematics, computer science, engineering, law, economics and philosophy.<ref name="Hertig2015"/> 
The focus according to Wilmer is "blockchain technology research."<ref name="Geekwire"></ref>
It is funded by [[Coin Center]], a nonprofit.<ref name="Pitchron">{{cite web |last1=Blake|first1=Sharon|title=Cryptocurrency Research Finds a Home at Pitt with Ledger Journal|url=https://www.chronicle.pitt.edu/story/cryptocurrency-research-finds-home-pitt-ledger-journal |website=Pitt Chronicle |accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=4 May 2017}}</ref> 

The journal is [[open access]].  It is published by the [[Hillman Library#University Library System|University Library System]] of the [[University of Pittsburgh]] and is cosponsored by the [[University of Pittsburgh Press]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dotson |first1=Kyt |title=The University of Pittsburgh is now home to Ledger: the first Bitcoin-only academic journal |url=http://siliconangle.com/blog/2015/09/15/the-university-of-pittsburgh-is-now-home-to-ledger-the-first-bitcoin-only-academic-journal/ |website=siliconangle.com |accessdate=12 January 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170112102850/http://siliconangle.com/blog/2015/09/15/the-university-of-pittsburgh-is-now-home-to-ledger-the-first-bitcoin-only-academic-journal/ |archivedate=12 January 2017 |date=16 September 2015}}</ref><ref name="Pitchron">{{cite web |last1=Blake|first1=Sharon|title=Cryptocurrency Research Finds a Home at Pitt with Ledger Journal|url=https://www.chronicle.pitt.edu/story/cryptocurrency-research-finds-home-pitt-ledger-journal |website=Pitt Chronicle |accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=4 May 2017}}</ref>

== Creation ==

The idea for the journal was born out of a discussion between [[editor-in-chief|managing editors]] Peter R. Rizun and Christopher E. Wilmer, on the [[bitcoin]] forum bitcointalk.org.

Wilmer envisioned ledger as a journal for "people passionate about the technology, to publish their research."<ref name="NPR-WESA90.5">{{cite web |last1=Nootbar|first1=Mark|title='Ledger' Becomes First Academic Journal Dedicated To Blockchain – The Technology Behind Bitcoin|url=https://www.wesa.fm/post/ledger-becomes-first-academic-journal-dedicated-blockchain-technology-behind-bitcoin#stream/0 |website=NPR (WESA 90.5FM)|accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=11 April 2017}}</ref>
Wilmer called into question the reliability of 'white papers' that became common in the cryptocurrency boom.
According to Wilmer, the Ledger Journal receives two to four submissions a week, and many are of poor quality.
“Occasionally we get submissions with no citations."<ref name="Wired-20180718">{{cite magazine |last1=CHEN|first1=SOPHIA |title=Why You Can't Trust More Cryptocurrency White Papers|url=https://www.wired.com/story/why-you-cant-trust-most-cryptocurrency-white-papers/ |magazine=Wired|accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=18 July 2018}}</ref>
Wilmer's vision for Ledger was to use a more a traditional peer review system.<ref name="Wired-20180718"></ref>

A call for papers was issued on 15 September 2015 with the deadline set to 31 December 2015.  However, this was delayed while formalising the review process.  The inaugural issue was not published until December 2016.<ref name="Hertig2015">{{cite web |last1=Hertig |first1=Alyssa |title=Introducing Ledger, the First Bitcoin-Only Academic Journal |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/introducing-ledger-the-first-bitcoin-only-academic-journal/ |website=motherboard.vice.com |publisher=Vice Media |access-date=10 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170110172807/http://motherboard.vice.com/read/introducing-ledger-the-first-bitcoin-only-academic-journal |archive-date=10 January 2017 |url-status=live |date=15 September 2015}}</ref>

== Related persons and organizations ==

Rizun is a physicist and entrepreneur, who lives in Vancouver, Canada.<ref name="PittNews">{{cite web |last1=Carr |first1=Annemarie |title=Pitt to publish first academic journal on Bitcoin|url=https://pittnews.com/article/63374/news/pitt-to-publish-first-academic-journal-on-bitcoin/ |website=PittNews.com |publisher= |accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=28 September 2015}}</ref>

Wilmer is an assistant professor in the [[Swanson School of Engineering]]’s Chemical & Petroleum Engineering Department.<ref name="Geekwire">{{cite web |last1=BISHOP |first1=TODD |title=Q&A: The inside story of 'Ledger,' the academic journal for blockchain and cryptocurrency research|url=https://www.geekwire.com/2018/qa-inside-story-ledger-academic-journal-blockchain-cryptocurrency-research/ |website=Geekwire |accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=13 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="WESA-2">{{cite web |last1=Kovash |first1=Sarah |title=Is It A Big Deal That Sheetz Now Has Bitcoin ATMs?|url=http://wesa.org/post/it-big-deal-sheetz-now-has-bitcoin-atms |website=NPR-WESA|accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=30 July 2019}}</ref>
He is the author of ''Bitcoin for befuddled''. Wilmer first used bitcoin to purchase honey caramels from a beekeeper.<ref name="PittMag">{{cite web |last1=Wiedel|first1=Susan|title=Pitt Chat with Chris Wilmer: A Pitt professor breaks down the basics of blockchains, the tech behind cryptocurrency|url=https://www.pittmag.pitt.edu/news/pitt-chat-chris-wilmer |website=PittMag Winter 2019|accessdate=20 January 2020 |date=}}</ref>

The University of Pittsburgh was featured in the documentary ''The Rise and Rise of Bitcoin''.<ref name="Geekwire"></ref>
